- When sentiment is consistently bullish (1.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects or fails to adjust downward; apply a dampening factor to subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (0.00) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast slightly to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model tends to lag in capturing true price momentum — especially after a strong bullish sentiment run — so add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment influence to forecast adjustment.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to prioritize recent sentiment shifts over historical trends.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a downward bias of 1–3% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to reflect recent volatility decay.
